cards.text: The time is drawing near for David, king of Israel, to die, and he calls in his son Solomon for one last talk. David says, "I am about to go the way of all the earth. So be strong and prove yourself a man."

cards.question: Along with being strong, what else does David charge his son Solomon to do?
David tells Solomon to keep God's commands as written in the Law of Moses, so that he may ___ in all he does and wherever he turns.

cards.text: David says it's also so the LORD may fulfill a promise He made to David himself. No pressure, son, NONE at all.

cards.question: What did the LORD promise David?

answers.text: A man of his line on Israel's throne
A palace that would never fall
Peace with every nation around him

cards.question: True or false: The LORD's promise to David held no matter how David's descendants lived.

cards.text: Then the goodbye speech turns into a to-do list. David brings up Joab son of Zeruiah, the commander of David's own army, and what Joab did to Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, two commanders of Israel's armies.

cards.question: What does David say Joab did to Abner and Amasa?
David says Joab stained his belt and sandals with the blood of war. Then he tells Solomon to act according to his wisdom. What should Solomon do about Joab?

answers.text: Not let him die in peace

cards.text: FINALLY, a name on David's list you'd actually WANT to be on. David tells Solomon to show loving devotion to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite.

cards.question: True or false: David wants Barzillai's sons to be among those who eat at Solomon's table.
David says Barzillai's sons stood by him when he ___ Solomon's brother Absalom.

cards.text: My whole goodbye from the drawer fit on the back of one takeout menu, and David's has a SECOND PAGE. Next name: Shimei son of Gera, a Benjamite from Bahurim.
Shimei called down bitter curses against David the day David went to Mahanaim. Bitter curses at the KING, and friend, I can't even talk back to an oven timer.

cards.question: True or false: When Shimei came down to meet David at the Jordan, David swore to him by the LORD never to put him to the sword.
David tells Solomon he's a wise man who will know what to do with Shimei. What does David want for Shimei's gray head?

answers.text: Brought down to Sheol in blood
Left to go down in peace

cards.text: And with that, the king's last words are spoken. David rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David.

cards.question: True or false: David reigned over Israel for forty years, all of them in Jerusalem.
Solomon sat on the throne of his father David, and his kingdom was ___ established.

cards.text: David's chapter just closed, and Solomon's holding the pen now. Don't go anywhere, friend, because that ink isn't even dry.

findings.problem: The correct answer is the only explicitly biblical, LORD-centered option. The distractors sound like generic or exaggerated advice, so the right answer stands out instead of sounding like the others.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker distinguish "firmly" from "barely" or "briefly." The blank therefore asks for the unseen wording of verse 12 rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Discovery questions are not limited to a few here. Cards 8, 11, 12, 15, 18 and 19 quiz unrevealed details, and card 2 likewise gives no passage-based basis for choosing its answer. Most of the stop's choices consequently depend on prior knowledge, answer wording or luck rather than reasoning from the earlier cards.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
